facts.text: Stoneham was first settled by colonists in 1634, originally part of Charlestown before becoming its own town.
The town is the birthplace of Olympic figure‑skating medalist Nancy Kerrigan, who grew up in Stoneham before competing in 1992 and 1994.
Stoneham’s historic shoe‑manufacturing, tanneries, and box factories are celebrated in the town seal, a nod to its industrial past.
The Stoneham Historical Society, founded in 1922, operates a museum that houses artifacts chronicling nearly a century of local history.
Stoneham is home to the Stone Zoo, a small but popular wildlife park that attracts visitors from the greater Boston area.
The town’s first meetinghouse and Burying Ground were both erected in 1726, with the cemetery later listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
